newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt firms, Trump trips in junk mart.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt firms, Trump trips in junk mart.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds followed Treasuries to higher ground in a shortened session Friday, and dealers reported little breakdown in spreads.
Trump Castle debt declined in the high-yield arena, meanwhile, after reports indicated Rank Organisation Plc will not follow through on an expected $50 million investment in the Atlantic City casino.
A press conference slated for Nov 19 that was expected to detail the move to change the casino's theme into a Hard Rock Casino Hotel was postponed due to "logistical" reasons.
Trump Castle notes traded within the 87-1/2 to 88 range and closed with an 86 bid, down six points from Wednesday.
The market was closed Thursday for U.S. Thanksgiving.
Back in high-grades, dealers said few trades took place and the few players who were at their desks said next week's brisk new issue calendar was the only fodder for conversation.

"There should be a lot of people jumping into the market before we get more entrenched in the holiday season," an investment grades trader said, adding it took little finagling to get even the largest deals done.
Lackluster activity left some spreads to widen but players insisited that was due more to apathy than to market weakness.

Big buying from Japanese accounts took U.S. Treasuries higher overnight, analysts said. Follow-through buying in the U.S. market pushed the benchmark 30-year T-bond yield down to 6.36 percent, its lowest since early March.

Turning to the broad high-yield market, traders reported a similar post-holiday malaise and strong market fundamentals. Prices were firmer across the board but there were few trades to prove the gains, traders said.
More important, traders said, was the expected $1.5 billion in high-yield issuance for this week and next.
PSA's Bond Market Trade Association recommended a 1400 EST/1900 GMT close for the U.S. Treasury and related markets following the Thanksgiving Day holiday.
